correctness.rationale: The discrete cycle Fourier ratio gives mean antipodal square distance ≤c^{-1} times mean neighbor squares with c=sin²(pi/(2m)). For two fiber labels, midpoint/half-difference decomposition and the cross-fiber antipodal pairs force D²≥(m+λ)²c/(1+λ²c) for arbitrary Hilbert embeddings. The regular polygon plus orthogonal regular simplex has squared pair distances D²(sin²(kθ)/c+ελ²); the stated sine concavity bounds verify both Lipschitz directions for k=0..m and ε=0,1 when 0<λ≤1. Independent tests verified all pair types for 132 parameter pairs. The proof, not these finite tests, gives the uniform all-r statement.

originality.rationale: Linial and Magen (Theorem 3.5, 2000) prove optimal standard embeddings for unweighted Cartesian products of cycles, covering λ=1 for a two-point fiber. The paper does not introduce the independently weighted complete-fiber factor 0<λ<1. Cioabă et al. concern distance-regular graph metrics, not this weighted family.
residual_risks: Unindexed weighted-product SDP theorem could give the whole λ family.
A unit-weight endpoint is already covered for r=2; no novelty claimed there.
Restricted to even cycle, complete fiber, λ≤1, not general weights.
